title: Ordinary finite coefficient pullback agrees with tensor-unit coordinates
statement: Let A be any commutative ring and f:X→Y any morphism of schemes. Use the ordinary finite derived coefficient objects and their canonical pullback comparison of [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. Under the canonical degree-zero tensor-unit identifications, (ordinaryFiniteUnitPullback A f).hom equals (leftDerivedUpperStarUnitIso (ModuleCat A) f).hom. No finiteness, annihilator, invertibility or nonempty hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The proved source-library identity singleFunctorObjUnitIso_inv identifies the inverse unit comparison with identity. Its inverse-hom identity therefore identifies its hom with identity as well. This is a two-line isomorphism cancellation in arbitrary coefficient categories.

Substitute these two identities into constantUnitPullback_unit from the etale section unit normalization. The functor map of identity and the two identity compositions cancel, identifying the constantSinglePullbackIso component with the monoidal unit map. Specialize to ModuleCat A. The ordinary finite pullback component is that same constant comparison by ordinaryFiniteUnitPullback_hom_eq_constant, giving the result.

theorem ordinaryFiniteUnitPullback_eq_unitCoordinates
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    (ordinaryFiniteUnitPullback A f).hom =
      (leftDerivedUpperStarUnitIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) f).hom
